status: DIAGNOSIS ONLY, no code changed. The cause is located and measured on two binaries; the fix needs one more producer trace, named below
classification: discovery; why no torpedo aircraft in this project has ever reached the aim tick
finding: All five of USN01's Mavs fly into the water at about 141 m/s roughly eleven seconds into the run. Every symptom the stream was chasing is downstream of that: the approach stops at 124 ticks because run_torpedo_task_arm_009d4850 returns on command_target_plus_one == 0 once the aircraft is gone; min == last == 3928.5 m because it closed 330.7 m and then died; aim_ticks=0 because the in-range latch wants range < 2200 m; and 009D2287, 007BBBA0 and 007EEF30 are all downstream of an aim stage that never runs. The heading error reached 0.000 rad, so steering was correct.
proximate_cause: The commanded run-in altitude is 12 m and the pitch demand is exactly -pi/3 rad, held from 800 m to the sea. The aim tick's floor is approach+78h + approach+74h at 009D1631: +78h is TorpReleaseAlt 12.0 (correct for what it is) and +74h is 0.00.
root_cause: OPEN, and the first candidate is withdrawn. 009D3489-009D34AE stores alt_floor_74 = ctl+398h only when ctl+398h < 100.0 (FLD [ECX+398h], FCOMIP against the double at 00D7A220, JBE skips), and the host feeds that field 500.0f, so the store never fires and +74h stays 0. That looked like the defect until 009C89CE was read: on the dive-bomb path +398h is tuning+4CCh plus a jitter, and tuning+4C0h..+4D8h is the dive bomb's cruising-altitude block, so a value above 100 is probably normal and alt_floor_74 = 0 probably is too. A commanded band of 12 m is then a plausible torpedo RELEASE altitude rather than a defect. What is unexplained, and is now the question, is the descent: pitch_demand is exactly -pi/3 rad and is held constant over more than 700 m, which is the shape of a clamp rather than of a computed slope, and the aircraft never flares. See the Correction section of the doc.

cause: LOCATED, section 9 of the doc. The attackrun tick's step 4 calls command_altitude_and_throttle(nullptr, alt_margin_78 + alt_floor_74, 0.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f) - both range arguments zero - so 009FBA50's span = max(range_high - range_low, 0) is zero, its bias term span * scale * class+518h is dead, and the commanded altitude is the bare 12 m. 009FB800's dive arm then returns -min(class_drop_angle * t, limit) with t clamped to reference by an 788 m error, so it saturates at the limit, which is -pi/3 to four decimals. The demand is the arm working correctly on a command it should never have been given. The move-to tick's own glide slope, in the same file, passes a real pair (range_low = the speed field selected by the approach clock, range_high = the distance) and produces a sloping descent; it never runs for these aircraft, and the log confirms it - there is not one `glide census` line, only `descent census` lines.
remaining_work: Read 009D07B0 step 4's argument setup from the listing and pass the real range pair. The host's zeros are a placeholder, not a reading. Do not assume the move-to pair is the right answer: 009D48CF fills the move-to ranges from approach+7Ch/+80h, which docs/TORPEDO_APPROACH_UPDATE.md establishes are commanded SPEEDS selected by the approach clock, so whatever 009D07B0 passes has to come from its own listing.
superseded_next_step: Start from the descent law, not the altitude field. pitch_demand is -1.0472 rad, which is -pi/3 to four decimals, held constant over more than 700 m of descent while the same census line prints drop_angle=0.4014 and climb_1ec=0.1854, neither of which the aircraft flies, and the aircraft never flares (pitch tracks the demand to -1.0396 at 62 m and the next sample is under the water). Find what writes that demand and why it is a constant rather than the glide slope docs/TORPEDO_MOVETO_TICK.md reconstructs, and what should level the aircraft at the band. docs/TORPEDO_RUN_IN_DESCENT.md is the other document on that path. Whether read_control_block is also passing the wrong key for +398h is unproven either way and is secondary: no producer of +398h on the torpedo path has been located at all, since 009D4A70 only reads it.
